Abstract
               
                  Summary
                  We developed 2DImpute, an imputation method for correcting false zeros (known as dropouts) in single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. It features preventing excessive correction by predicting the false zeros and imputing their values by making use of the interrelationships between both genes and cells in the expression matrix. We showed that 2DImpute outperforms several leading imputation methods by applying it on datasets from various scRNA-seq protocols.
               
               
                  Availability and implementation
                  The R package of 2DImpute is freely available at GitHub (https://github.com/zky0708/2DImpute).
               
               
                  Contact
                  d.anastassiou@columbia.edu
               
               
                  Supplementary information
                  Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

Abstract

Summary
We developed 2DImpute, an imputation approach for correcting false zeros, or dropouts, in single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. It aims to avoid overcorrection by predicting false zeros and imputing their values while leveraging relationships among both genes and cells in the expression matrix. We demonstrated that 2DImpute outperforms several leading imputation methods when applied to datasets from a range of scRNA-seq protocols.

Availability and implementation
The 2DImpute R package is freely available on GitHub (https://github.com/zky0708/2DImpute).

Contact
d.anastassiou@columbia.edu

Supplementary information
Supplementary data are available online at Bioinformatics.
